headline: Your One Step GPS waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing every US commercial fleet into the right One Step GPS offer: ELD compliance, AI dashcams, no-contract scaling, or the published-price teardown. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Nico Photos.
productSummary: One Step GPS (onestepgps.com) is a cloud-based fleet management SaaS platform, web app plus iOS and Android, covering real-time GPS tracking, driver behavior monitoring, fleet safety, AI dashcams, ELD compliance, maintenance management, and asset tracking. Verified from onestepgps.com/about/company-facts-data: 20,000+ active commercial fleets across many industries; approximately 6% of the Fortune 100; 4.9/5 average rating across 3,600+ public reviews; 99% CSAT, 99% first-call resolution, 4.34 minutes average time to resolution; 99.99% platform uptime; 1-30 second location refresh; ~6 feet GPS accuracy; 3 years of historical data included. Published flat-rate pricing: $13.95 per vehicle/month (GPS), $20.95 per vehicle/month (ELD with GPS, being the $7.00 per driver ELD add-on on top of the $13.95 base), $29.95 per vehicle/month (AI dashcam with GPS), plus a one-time $20 activation fee per GPS or ELD device. No long-term contracts, no early cancellation fee, no equipment purchase fees (devices are loaned and returned at end of service), lifetime hardware warranty, 100-day money-back guarantee. 82+ marketplace integrations (WEX, Fuelman, Coast, ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro, Fleetio, MaintainX, UpKeep, 28+ insurance partners including Aon, Alliant, Amwins, Berkley, HUB, Kinsale, RLI, plus OEM feeds from John Deere JDLink, Vision Link, Stellantis) and a free documented open API. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. Support is 100% US-based and in-house, Monday to Friday 5am-5pm Pacific. Awards: Inc. 5000 five consecutive years (2021-2025), 2025 American Business Awards Grand Stevie and Gold Stevie for Customer Service, Capterra 2026 Shortlist #2 in Fleet Management, Capterra Best Ease of Use 5.0/5. Fleet size bands are canonical to One Step GPS: Small 1-50 vehicles, Mid-sized 51-250, Large 250+.
coreInsight: One Step GPS is not competing on features, it is competing on terms. Their own 13-provider, 110-data-point benchmark says 85% of fleet providers do not publish clear pricing, 77% require a contract (most multi-year), and 92% gate features behind plan tiers, and Berg Insight names One Step GPS as the only one of the 15 largest North American providers by installed base operating entirely without long-term contracts. So the TAM does not need educating on GPS tracking. It needs a reason to move now. The single routing signal is fleet_record_state: what the public FMCSA record already says about a fleet's compliance heat, safety exposure, and unit growth. The FMCSA Company Census plus the SMS violation and crash files deliver the entire TAM (about 2.1 million active USDOT registrations) and the routing signal in one free pull, with power units, drivers, address, and phone already attached. Industry (construction, trades, delivery, landscaping, towing, transit, government) is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall.

signalReasons: The FMCSA Company Census File on data.transportation.gov is the TAM and the routing signal in one free pull. FMCSA A&I Registration Statistics puts active motor carrier companies with USDOT numbers at roughly 2.1 million (snapshots in 2026 range from about 2.08M to 2.23M depending on file date), with power units, driver count, legal name, DBA, address, and phone already on the record. No paid enrichment is needed before a lead is routed.

The SMS violation, inspection, and crash files attach to the same USDOT number, so compliance heat and safety exposure are observable presence signals, not inferred absence. A recorded hours-of-service violation proves the logging problem existed at a roadside stop. That is exactly the reliability bar the waterfall method requires, unlike guessing which telematics vendor a fleet uses today.

The ladder maps one-to-one onto One Step GPS's published offers: FMCSA-registered ELD/HOS at $20.95 with GPS for the HOS tier, AI dashcams at $29.95 with in-cab coaching and 28+ insurance integrations for the safety tier, $13.95 flat with add-and-drop devices and no penalty for the growth tier, and the published-pricing story for the catch-all. Every tier's value prop is lifted from onestepgps.com/about/company-facts-data.

Industry and fleet size are merge tags, not a second waterfall. One Step GPS explicitly serves construction, field services, government, transportation and logistics, oil and gas, last-mile delivery, agriculture and mining, rental vehicles and equipment, passenger transit, and landscaping, and it publishes its own fleet size bands (Small 1-50, Mid-sized 51-250, Large 250+). Those slot into copy after routing.

sources.name: FMCSA MCMIS Company Census File (data.transportation.gov)
sources.delivers: The TAM spine plus in_tam, usdot_number, power_units, driver_count, legal name, DBA, physical address, phone, and MCS-150 filing date. Free bulk download. About 2.1 million active USDOT registrations, of which roughly 701k are for-hire with interstate authority and about 1.48M are private carriers.

sources.name: FMCSA SMS BASIC percentiles + inspection and violation files
sources.delivers: hos_violation_12mo, hos_basic_percentile, unsafe_driving_basic_percentile, and the specific violation codes (395.x hours-of-service and ELD, speeding, reckless, distracted). This is the Tier 1 and Tier 2 routing signal, keyed on the same USDOT number.

sources.name: FMCSA crash file / SAFER Company Snapshot
sources.delivers: crash_count_24mo and the human-readable snapshot used for QA on any account before a send. Confirms the record state a first line will quote.

sources.name: MCS-150 revision history (census deltas over time)
sources.delivers: power_unit_growth_pct and new_authority_date for Tier 3. Comparing two census snapshots is free and shows which fleets actually added units rather than which ones say they are growing.

sources.name: Google Maps / Places by trade category and metro
sources.delivers: The non-DOT half of the catch-all: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, pest control, towing, mobile services, and equipment rental fleets that operate vehicles but never file with FMCSA. Returns name, phone, website, and location count in the same pull.

sources.name: Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Nav (after routing)
sources.delivers: buyer_title and work email for an already-routed account: Owner, Fleet Manager, Director of Operations, Safety Director, VP Operations, Fleet Supervisor. Contact resolution last, never the TAM spine on its own.

sources.name: Indeed / LinkedIn job posts (optional Tier 3 confirmation)
sources.delivers: hiring_drivers as a secondary growth confirmation, and any incumbent telematics tool named in a dispatcher or fleet-manager job description. Presence only. Never route on the absence of a named tool.

sources.name: One Step GPS customer suppression list
sources.delivers: already_customer exclusion, supplied by One Step GPS before launch. With 20,000+ active fleets on the platform this matters more than usual. Suppress, do not tier.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND NOT already_customer AND (hos_violation_12mo >= 1 OR hos_basic_percentile is over the FMCSA intervention threshold)
routingRules.why: A government record already proves the logs failed at a roadside stop. Strongest intent, and there is a clock on it: the percentile keeps drawing inspections and the insurance renewal prices off it. One Step GPS answers with FMCSA-registered ELD/HOS at $20.95 per vehicle per month with GPS, automated IFTA, DVIR workflows, no contract, no early cancellation fee, and a 100-day money-back guarantee.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND NOT already_customer AND NOT Tier 1 AND (unsafe_driving_basic_percentile is over threshold OR crash_count_24mo >= 1 OR a speeding, reckless, or distracted-driving violation appears on a recent inspection)
routingRules.why: The safety record is public and the insurer prices off it, but the fleet has no video and no per-driver scorecard to defend or coach with. One Step GPS answers with AI dashcams at $29.95 per vehicle per month: dual-facing HD, AI detection of phone use, tailgating, drowsiness and distracted driving, real-time in-cab coaching, automated safety scorecards, and 28+ insurance integrations.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND NOT already_customer AND NOT Tier 1 AND NOT Tier 2 AND (power_unit_growth_pct >= 20 vs the prior MCS-150 filing OR new_authority_date within the last 24 months OR hiring_drivers = true)
routingRules.why: Adding units is exactly when an incumbent quotes a fresh multi-year term per vehicle, which is the worst moment to sign one. One Step GPS answers with $13.95 flat, $20 one-time activation, no equipment purchase fee, unlimited admin users, self-install OBD-II devices, and the ability to add or pull devices at any time with no penalty including seasonal off-season returns.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND NOT already_customer AND none of the above (remaining FMCSA census fleets plus non-DOT commercial fleets sourced from Maps and Apollo)
routingRules.why: No event to point at, so lead with the category default instead. One Step GPS's own 13-provider, 110-data-point benchmark found 85% do not publish clear pricing, 77% require a contract and most are multi-year, and 92% gate features behind plan tiers. The soft offer is the published-rate teardown: $13.95 flat, no contract, no equipment fee, 100-day money-back, 4.9/5 across 3,600+ reviews. Mandatory 100% TAM coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Hours-of-service violation on the public record
tiers.trigger: One or more hours-of-service or ELD violations (395.x) on a roadside inspection in the last 12 months, or an HOS Compliance BASIC over the FMCSA intervention threshold
tiers.pain: The logs already failed at the roadside. The BASIC percentile keeps pulling more inspections, the next stop risks an out-of-service order, and the insurance renewal prices off the same public score. Whatever ELD they run is not producing clean logs, and switching mid-term usually means paying out the rest of a multi-year contract.
tiers.valueProp: FMCSA-registered ELD/HOS at $7.00 per driver on top of the $13.95 GPS base, so $20.95 per vehicle per month published, with automated IFTA reporting and DVIR/inspection workflows in the same login. No contract, no early cancellation fee, no equipment purchase fee, lifetime device warranty, 100-day money-back guarantee, and 100% US-based in-house support at 99% first-call resolution and 4.34 minutes average time to resolution.
tiers.dataSource: FMCSA SMS HOS Compliance BASIC + inspection and violation files, keyed on the census USDOT number
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - a government record proves the pain and there is a renewal clock on it
tiers.accounts: est. ~17,000 accounts (GTMx estimate, not an FMCSA-published figure)

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Safety or crash exposure, no HOS flag
tiers.trigger: Not Tier 1, and an Unsafe Driving BASIC over threshold, or one or more reportable crashes in the last 24 months, or a speeding, reckless, or distracted-driving violation on a recent inspection
tiers.pain: The safety record is public and it is what the insurer prices off at renewal, but there is no footage and no per-driver scorecard. Every claim comes down to a driver's word, and coaching is anecdotal because nobody can rank who is actually risky.
tiers.valueProp: AI dashcams at $29.95 per vehicle per month: dual-facing HD with an optional driver-facing camera, AI event detection for cell phone use, eating and drinking, smoking, tailgating, distracted driving and drowsiness, real-time audible and visible in-cab coaching, and cloud footage for review. Automated safety scorecards rank speeding, hard cornering, acceleration and braking across drivers, groups and the whole fleet. 28+ insurance integrations including Aon, Alliant, Amwins, Berkley, HUB, Kinsale and RLI. No contract, 100-day money-back guarantee.
tiers.dataSource: FMCSA SMS Unsafe Driving BASIC + crash file, same USDOT key
tiers.replyDensity: High - the exposure is public and the renewal date is a hard deadline

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Fleet growing or newly registered, clean safety record
tiers.trigger: Not Tier 1 or 2, and power units up 20% or more versus the prior MCS-150 filing, or USDOT authority granted in the last 24 months, or actively hiring drivers and technicians
tiers.pain: Growth is the moment the incumbent asks for a fresh multi-year term on every new unit. A fleet whose vehicle count just moved 20% cannot honestly forecast 36 months of per-vehicle spend, and seasonal add-and-drop gets penalised under a standard term.
tiers.valueProp: $13.95 per vehicle per month published flat, $20 one-time activation per device, no equipment purchase fee (devices are loaned and returned at end of service), unlimited admin users with role-based permissions at no extra charge, 3 years of history included, and devices can be added or pulled at any time with no penalty, including returning units at no charge during an off-season. OBD-II plug-in devices self-install in under a minute. Berg Insight: of the 15 largest North American fleet management providers by installed base, One Step GPS is the only one operating entirely without long-term contracts.
tiers.dataSource: MCS-150 census deltas between snapshots, plus optional Indeed / LinkedIn hiring confirmation
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - real timing signal, but no penalty clock like Tiers 1 and 2

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Every remaining US commercial fleet, DOT and non-DOT
tiers.trigger: Any remaining in-TAM commercial fleet running 3+ vehicles with no Tier 1-3 record state, including the non-DOT trades fleets (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, pest control, towing, mobile services, equipment rental) that never appear on the FMCSA census
tiers.pain: No specific event, just the category default. Getting a straight price out of a fleet provider is the hard part: One Step GPS's own 13-provider, 110-data-point benchmark found 85% do not publish clear pricing, 77% require a contract and most are multi-year, and 92% gate features behind plan tiers.
tiers.valueProp: The whole offer as the hook. $13.95 per vehicle per month published, no contract, no early cancellation fee, no equipment purchase fee, lifetime hardware warranty, 100-day money-back guarantee, unlimited admin users, 3 years of history, 30+ prebuilt reports, maintenance scheduling by mileage or engine hours, geofence and after-hours alerts, 82+ integrations and a free documented open API. 20,000+ fleets, approximately 6% of the Fortune 100, 4.9/5 across 3,600+ public reviews, 100% US-based in-house support.
tiers.dataSource: Remaining FMCSA census records plus Google Maps trade-category scrape and Apollo contact resolution
tiers.replyDensity: Lowest - broadest list, softest CTA, highest volume

campaigns.name: HOS violation on the record (compliance-led)
campaigns.filter: in_tam + hos_violation_12mo >= 1 or HOS BASIC over threshold + not already_customer
campaigns.strategy: Open by naming {{violation_signal}} straight off the SMS record, poke the renewal and out-of-service clock, then trade the published $20.95 ELD-with-GPS number plus no contract and the 100-day money-back guarantee for a one-word reply. Offer is the ELD Switch Sheet.
campaigns.overview: Highest intent route. Quote only what the public record actually shows. Never claim to know which ELD vendor they run today or what their contract says.

campaigns.name: HOS violation (terms-led A/B variant)
campaigns.filter: Same Tier 1 filter, alternate Day 0 copy only
campaigns.strategy: Chaos-test variant. Drop the violation-first opener and lead with the benchmark instead: 77% of the 13 providers One Step GPS benchmarked require a contract, most multi-year, and 92% gate features behind tiers. Then land on $20.95 published for ELD with GPS. Same magnet.
campaigns.overview: Two variants on Tier 1 only, held to the same offer and CTA, so the test reads cleanly. Do not clone this variant downward until Tier 1 picks a winner.

campaigns.name: Safety exposure and no footage
campaigns.filter: in_tam + Unsafe Driving BASIC over threshold or crash_count_24mo >= 1 + no Tier 1 match
campaigns.strategy: Name {{safety_signal}} from the public record, poke the insurance-renewal and no-evidence pain, then offer the Dashcam Exoneration Brief: $29.95 per vehicle, AI event detection, real-time in-cab coaching, automated scorecards, 28+ insurance integrations.
campaigns.overview: Second exclusive route. Copy is about defending the record they already have, not a dashcam explainer. Keep the tone matter-of-fact, never accusatory about crashes.

campaigns.name: Growing fleet, no term to sign
campaigns.filter: in_tam + power_unit_growth_pct >= 20 or authority < 24 months or hiring drivers + no Tier 1-2 match
campaigns.strategy: Lead with {{growth_signal}} from the census delta, poke the multi-year term that lands on every new unit, then offer the No-Contract Scaling Sheet: $13.95 flat, $20 activation, add or drop devices with no penalty, unlimited users, Berg Insight's only-one-without-contracts line.
campaigns.overview: Third exclusive route. {{fleet_size}} and {{industry}} are merge tags. Do not invent a savings figure for their specific fleet.

campaigns.name: Published price vs the category (whole offer)
campaigns.filter: in_tam + 3+ vehicles + no Tier 1-3 record state, DOT and non-DOT
campaigns.strategy: Billboard the whole offer. 85% of providers do not publish clear pricing, 77% require a contract, 92% gate features. One Step GPS publishes $13.95, no contract, no equipment fee, 100-day money-back, 4.9/5 across 3,600+ reviews. Offer is the Fleet Pricing Teardown.
campaigns.overview: Mandatory catch-all for 100% TAM coverage. Softest CTA in the cascade. Non-fleet local businesses stay out of this list entirely.

campaigns.name: Catch-all A/B: what the flat rate includes
campaigns.filter: Same catch-all filter, alternate Day 0 copy only
campaigns.strategy: Variant that skips the pricing-opacity stat and leads with inclusion instead: unlimited admin users, 3 years of history, 30+ reports, maintenance scheduling, geofence and after-hours alerts, 82+ integrations and a free open API, all inside the same $13.95. Same magnet.
campaigns.overview: Only two variants at a time on the catch-all. Vary the opener, hold the offer and CTA constant.

launchPlan: Confirm in_tam: US commercial fleet operators running 3+ vehicles. One Step GPS states no minimum fleet size and serves single-vehicle operators, but 3+ is the outbound economics gate. Non-fleet businesses and consumer vehicle tracking stay out entirely, and One Step GPS is explicit that it is not a consumer GPS product.

Pull the FMCSA MCMIS Company Census File from data.transportation.gov for the TAM spine, then join the SMS BASIC percentiles, inspection and violation files, and the crash file on usdot_number. Diff two census snapshots to derive power_unit_growth_pct. All free, no paid enrichment before routing.

Scrape Google Maps by trade category and metro (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, landscaping, pest control, towing, mobile services, equipment rental) to build the non-DOT half of the catch-all, since those fleets never file with FMCSA.

Apply the One Step GPS customer suppression list before anything sends. With 20,000+ active fleets on the platform this is not optional, and cold-emailing a current customer is the fastest way to lose the account's trust.

Launch Tier 1 only until reply density is clear, target 1 positive per 150 to 300. Do not launch any tier under ~1,500 contacts. Per-tier account counts on this page are GTMx estimates of how the TAM splits, not FMCSA-published figures. Do not put an estimated tier count in an email.
Add Tier 2 safety exposure once Tier 1 copy is stable, then Tier 3 growth, then the catch-all last since it carries the most volume and the softest CTA.

Resolve contacts with Apollo or Sales Nav only after an account is routed. Target Owner, Fleet Manager, Director of Operations, Safety Director, VP Operations. FMCSA already supplies a phone and address, so email enrichment is the only paid step.

Run two Day 0 variants on Tier 1 (violation-led vs terms-led) and two on the catch-all (pricing-opacity vs what-is-included). Hold the offer and CTA constant so the test reads. Do not clone a winner downward until the tier it was tested on has one.
